doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Soundscape and the Peter Watrous review
summary: His quintet debuted at Verna Gillis's loft Soundscape; Watrous's New York Times review led Lundvall to have him record with that group.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Verna Gillis was the owner of that place in the fifth floor. In order to get up there, you have to take a cargo elevator that sound like the sound of the Dracula castle [imitates sound]. [Jenkins laughs] It was scary man. It was scary because it was on the fifth floor, and you never know if it was going to open on the third floor and you were going to see Frankenstein or something. But I was lucky enough that that night, that I present my quintet there, a writer called Peter Watrous was there, and—I don’t know how he looks—but he was there and he like it. So he wrote a very nice article in, in the New York Times, so I had that afternoon, I got a meeting at CBS with a bunch of producers and all that, and Bruce Lundvall. So, I arrive there and I have a very vague idea of what I was going to do, you know. I was not prepared to do an LP for myself. I did not have a concert yet, I have some ideas. So when they arrive there, I say, “What are you all going to do?” And then somebody start talking about the Pop LP and all that, and Bruce Lundvall say, “Did you read what they say in the New York Times?” And I say, “No, what is that?” So he show it to me. I say, “Wow this is great! Why you don’t record with that group?”

The group was Ignacio Berroa on drums, Hilton Ruiz, Russell Blake on bass, Daniel Ponce on percussion, myself, and then as a guest artist, because I want to have Eddie Gomez; Eddie Gomez recorded a piece that I wrote called, “Basstronaut.” He record that piece; Mario Rivera play the alto too on a couple of tunes.
So Bruce said why don’t you record with that group?
With that group ‘you had great reviews; just record with that group.’
And what did the producers say?
Oh, they go for it, and it was really nice.
